joint.description: The rotor (hub-and-blade) balance-mass retention bolt: a single fastener, selected at assembly from a nine-member NAS6403 grip family, clamping an optional countersunk washer, zero or more stacked balancing masses, and a flat washer against whatever structure carries the tapped hole at this section. This is a genuinely different joint from the three already in this repo (pitch_link_to_pitch_plate, tan_link_to_pitch_plate, vpa_output_to_pitch_plate): those each use one fixed, as-drawn dash number; this one's own drawing note explicitly says to select a dash for correct grip length, which is exactly the reverse-engineering question this handoff was seeded with.
joint.places_note: Not a fixed count. General note 12 (JED02183) allows balance weights at 'ANY ONE OF 10 HOLE LOCATIONS' around the hub, used 'AS REQUIRED TO MEET BALANCE SPECIFICATION' up to 80 g per location and 200 g total. This stack models the grip-length question at ONE representative location, not a count of populated locations.

joint.clamped: From the bolt head down: the MS21299C3 countersunk washer (optional, AR, per JPS00094 5.5.3.a -- modelled here as present, matching what the section draws), zero or more stacked 216579-00X balancing masses (AR per note 12, up to 80 g combined per location -- NOT modelled, no part drawing gives a thickness; gap 1), the NAS1149V0332H flat washer, then whatever structure carries the tapped hole -- read from the balloon set as 216231-002 HUB AND BLADE ASSEMBLY, though the section also cuts through the VPA and tangential-link-mount assemblies at this same location and none of the three balloons here carries a dimension (gap 2). Retention is a blind tapped hole, not a nut: there is no MS9363/MS24665 at this joint, so the castellation-quantisation caveat that governs the other three 217755 joints does not apply here.
joint.question: Given whatever balance-mass configuration is actually installed at this location (per note 12, 0 to a stacked combination up to 80 g) and whatever structure the bolt is tapped into, does at least one of the nine as-drawn NAS6403 grip options (note 24: 'SELECT ONE FASTENER FROM PROVIDED OPTIONS AS REQUIRED FOR CORRECT GRIP LENGTH PER JPS00094 AND/OR AC43.13-1B') clamp the stack fully -- i.e. keep the receiving member from engaging the bolt's incomplete threads (JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5: 'The nut, nutplate, insert, part body, etc., shall not engage any incomplete threads of the bolt shank') -- across the tolerance range?
joint.scope: Grip length only, along the bolt axis, exactly as the other three 217755 joints in this repo. Deliberately out of scope: which of up to 10 balance-hole locations is used and how the 200 g total balance budget (JED02183) is allocated across them; torque (note 15: 2.26-2.82 Nm plus running torque per JPS00094); the safety-cable capture (note 7); diameter and hole fits; thread-engagement depth into the tapped member (a diametral/depth question, not a grip-length one). An omission below is a decision, not an oversight.
joint.identification_note: Not identified by fastener nomenclature -- identified by the drawing's OWN framing matching the handoff's, word for word. 217755 sheet 1 general note 24 reads 'SELECT ONE FASTENER FROM PROVIDED OPTIONS AS REQUIRED FOR CORRECT GRIP LENGTH PER JPS00094 AND/OR AC43.13-1B', which is the handoff's 'reverse-engineer the rotor fastener length stack' in the drawing's own words. Corroborating evidence: (1) this is the only 217755 joint with a genuine grip-SELECTION family (nine NAS6403 dash options, note 24) rather than one fixed as-drawn dash -- the other three joints (pitch link, tangential link, VPA output) each balloon a single dash number; (2) note 12 ties this joint to balance weights 'AS REQUIRED TO MEET BALANCE SPECIFICATIONS' on the hub-and-blade assembly, i.e. the rotating 'rotor', not the pitch-plate linkage the other three joints clamp; (3) the existing NAS1149V0332 hardware entry (authored before this handoff, for the pitch-link joint) already lists a balloon 'at SECTION T-T' among its assembly_status.balloons, an independent prior sighting of this same joint. A second 217755 candidate was considered and set aside: sheet 4 SECTION K-K retains 214849-003 SPINDLE SUBASSEMBLY with MS21250H03014 bolts at a single fixed .875 in grip (no dash family) plus bearing-preload shims (214935-001/-004/-005) -- a shim-selects-PRELOAD problem, not a select-the-grip-length problem, and its drawing carries no note analogous to 24. Ruled out; if Jason's screenshot names this joint instead once it lands, that comparison will say so.
joint.as_drawn_notes: General notes this joint's hardware carries, per 217755 sheet 1: note 7 (install a safety cable to capture the fastener per JPS00094), note 12 (balance-weight installation limits, JED02183), note 15 (dry install per JPS00094, torque 2.26-2.82 Nm plus running torque), note 24 (select fastener for correct grip length, quoted above).

notes: BUILT FROM SCRATCH. No source workbook exists for this joint (neither slice 1 nor the 260729 workbook analysed it), so there is no re-derivation section in the worksheet, no `workbook_cells` on any path or check, and no `[NOT IN WORKBOOK]` markers -- every check here is original. `kind: "workbook"` appears zero times, as SOP Step 5b requires.

THE STACK IS INCOMPLETE AND SAYS SO -- more so than the other three 217755 joints. Two members of the clamped column have no document at all: the balancing-mass thickness (only weight in grams is printed; no part drawing for 216579-002..-007) and the receiving structure's engagement thickness (216231-002 HUB AND BLADE ASSEMBLY and its neighbours are reference-only balloons with no dimension). Both are named gaps; neither is filled with a recalled or plausible number.

NINE-WAY GRIP FAMILY, NOT ONE FASTENER. Unlike the other three 217755 joints (each a single fixed as-drawn dash), this joint's own drawing note (24) says to SELECT a dash at assembly. This stack therefore models all nine as-drawn options and reports, per dash, the combined mass+structure thickness budget it can accommodate before shank-out would go negative -- not a single pass/fail verdict. All nine checks are `complete: false` by construction and read as budgets, exactly like pitch_link_to_pitch_plate's two checks.

OPTIONAL WASHER INCLUDED BY DEFAULT. MS21299C3 is ballooned 'AR'; JPS00094 5.5.3.a allows 0-3 such washers when a coarser bolt-length step is substituted for the exact grip needed. This stack includes exactly one (matching what SECTION T-T draws), so removing or doubling it shifts every check's budget by 1.6002 mm -- not modelled as a second configuration.

NO INVERTING ELEMENT AND NO CASTELLATION. The nine fastener elements are the only ones carrying lmc/mmc, and all are additive external lengths (max == mmc); there is no chamfer, relief or counterbore in this joint. The two washers carry null lmc/mmc, same convention as the other joints' zero-width washers -- there is no transcribed material condition to record. Retention here is a blind tapped hole, not a nut: no MS9363 slotted/castellated nut and no MS24665 cotter pin appear at this joint, so the castellated-grip quantisation caveat that governs the pitch-link and tangential-link joints does not apply.

JOINT IDENTITY IS INFERRED FROM THE DRAWING'S OWN LANGUAGE, NOT FROM NOMENCLATURE. See joint.identification_note for the full argument: general note 24's wording is the handoff's own framing, verbatim, and this is the only 217755 joint with a genuine grip-selection family.

Element order is head-to-tail as the section draws it: MS21299C3 washer, [balancing mass -- MISSING], NAS1149V0332H washer, [receiving-structure thickness -- MISSING]; the nine fastener grip options follow, one per check. Only the path term list is load-bearing for the arithmetic.
